outputs: The paper evaluates generated dialogue responses from chatbots in open-domain conversational settings.

changes_made.explanation: Normalized dataset name 'DailyDialog' and model name 'Sequence-to-Sequence'. Removed duplicate/abbreviated model names (GPT/BR/S2/BL/LC/KV/HF are abbreviations of full model names already listed). Simplified outputs description.
No automatic metrics used in this paper - paper explicitly states automatic metrics correlate poorly with human evaluations
Paper uses human judges, not LLMs, for evaluation

guideline: Annotators decide for each entity in a conversation segment whether it is human or bot (or unsure)
Annotators then rank which entity performs better on three features: fluency, sensibleness, and specificity

changes_made.explanation: Guideline and criteria were correctly extracted and are comprehensive

overall_notes: The extraction was generally accurate. Main changes were normalizing dataset names and removing redundant/abbreviated model names. The paper presents a novel human evaluation framework (Spot The Bot) for dialogue systems that uses bot-bot conversations instead of human-bot conversations, with human judges identifying which entities are bots vs humans.
